notes: v1.14.574 — THE DECK LOSES ITS TWO DUPLICATE PANELS. FIRST-DOOR Ship A slice A-2a. ⛔ SCOPE NARROWED BY MEASUREMENT, AND THE NARROWING IS REPORTED RATHER THAN PERFORMED QUIETLY: the owner confirmed A-2 as all of #cs-grid (rows 2,3,4,5), but row 4 — #cs-health to SYS — turned out NOT to be a relocation. The SYS panel is ROW-based (.hdr-agg-row: dot / name / value) while #cs-health is a Deck card, so re-homing it is a RENDERER REWRITE, not a move, and that is its own visible change. It becomes A-2b. This ship is the two deletions, the row-2 gate, and the grid. ⛔ ROW 3 (#cs-intel) DELETED, markup and renderer together: it was the NBA second face — its own comment said "one brain, two faces" — and .573 gave the brain a better one, the hero CTA plus the hero secondary line. A third face on one screen is the duplication section 1 exists against. ⛔ ROW 5 (#cs-build) DELETED, markup and renderer together: the hero already carries the deployment percentage and the rack count, and the picker it points at carries per-rack truth. A second aggregate on one screen is a second place for one fact to disagree. ⭐ BOTH RENDER BLOCKS WENT WITH THEIR MARKUP, DELIBERATELY. Leaving them would have created permanently-null getElementById lookups that fail safe and say nothing — the .473 shape, and exactly the debt .565 had to book as Ship 2b. ⚠ VERIFIED BEFORE CUTTING: the build rail ended in "if (!bb) return;" and was the TAIL of cs_renderDesktop, so nothing ran after it. Had anything followed, deleting #cs-build would have silently killed it — a null host becoming a skipped render with no warn and no toast. ⭐ ROW 2 (#cs-shiftbar) KEPT AND GATED, per owner ruling. It IS the shift-handoff door section 1 keeps, placed in #cs-grid by the ruling of 2026-08-14 because that container cannot be hidden by a composition rule. Re-homing was tried TWICE, into .lens and into .cs-microbar, and both were "present, wired, correct and dead" at 390. Only WHEN it speaks changes: hidden with no Master (A-S1 says the no-Master screen shows one headline, one action and nothing else, and a shift-end control on a device with no Master is a job that does not exist yet), visible once there is one. ⛔ THE DESKTOP GRID IS REDEFINED IN THE SAME STROKE, AND THAT IS WHY THIS SLICE IS CUT BY CONTAINER AND NOT BY ROW NUMBER: the deletions are markup and apply at EVERY width, while the placements are positional and desktop-only. Left alone, #cs-health would have floated at column 2 row 2 with an empty cell above and below it and the hero still spanning three rows — INVISIBLE on the phone the ship is verified on. DEBT BOOKED, NOT SILENTLY ACCRUED: the CSS for both deleted panels is still present — cs-intel and cs-build rules, plus .cs-irow/.cs-iorb/.cs-ititle/.cs-ibtn/.cs-iact and the .cs-step/.cs-bfoot/.cs-bphase rail styles — and CS_STEP_SHORT is now a zero-caller constant. LEFT DELIBERATELY: dead CSS in a single file costs nothing at runtime, and a sweep through it is cleanup disguised as progress on a ship that is about the surface, not the stylesheet. It is recorded here so it is a KNOWN debt rather than a discovered one, the way .565 booked its Ship 2b. ⚠ NOTE THE DISTINCTION FROM .473: nothing left behind is a CONTROL. A zero-caller constant and unmatched selectors are inert; a button wired to a function that no longer runs is not. No permanently-null getElementById lookups were left, because both render blocks went with their markup.
